Summarise LE8 scores with dplyr

Source: R/methods-summary.R
summarise.essential8_scores.Rd

With dplyr loaded, calling summarise() (or summarize()) on scores from score_le8() without any summary expressions returns the statistics in summary() as a data frame, one row per measure and group. Calls with expressions, such as summarise(scores, mean = mean(le8_composite_score)), are passed to dplyr unchanged.

Groups come from .by, or from the grouping of a grouped tibble passed to score_le8(). Because group_by() drops the essential8_scores class, use .by for grouped summaries of scored data, or restore the class with as_le8_scores().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'essential8_scores'
summarise(.data, ..., .by = NULL, .groups = NULL)

Arguments

.data

An essential8_scores object returned by score_le8().

...

Summary expressions. If any are supplied, the call is handled by dplyr::summarise().

.by

<tidy-select> Optional columns to group by for this summary.

.groups

Passed to dplyr::summarise() when ... is supplied. Otherwise ignored; the LE8 summary is always ungrouped.

Value

Without expressions, an ungrouped data frame of the same type as .data (a tibble for tibble input) with the grouping columns, measure (a factor: composite, then the eight components in AHA order), and the statistics n (available scores), n_missing, mean, sd, min, q25, median, q75, and max. With expressions, the result of dplyr::summarise().

See also

summary.essential8_scores(), tidy.essential8_scores()

Examples

library(dplyr)

adults <- read.csv(system.file(
  "extdata", "le8-adult-example.csv", package = "essential8"
))
scores <- adults |>
  select(!starts_with("expected_")) |>
  score_le8()

summarise(scores)
#>             measure  n n_missing    mean       sd min     q25  median      q75

# Ordinary dplyr summaries work as usual.
summarise(scores, mean_le8 = mean(le8_composite_score), .by = bmi_profile)
#>     bmi_profile mean_le8
#> 1       general 44.28571
#> 2 asian_pacific 54.37500
